scenes.title: Costco keeps 3¢ per $1
scenes.sub: So how does it make $9.2 billion?
scenes.sub_html: So how does it make $9.2 billion?

lines.say: Did you know Costco keeps only about three cents of profit from every dollar you spend there?
lines.show: Did you know Costco keeps only about 3¢ of profit from every $1 you spend there?

lines.say: So how did it still make nine point two billion dollars this past year?
lines.show: So how did it still make $9.2 billion this past year?

scenes.label: of stuff sold in one year

lines.say: Costco sold two hundred ninety-seven billion dollars of stuff in one year.
lines.show: Costco sold $297 billion of stuff in one year.

scenes.label: left after products, workers, stores and taxes

lines.say: After products, workers, stores and taxes, only about three cents per dollar is left.
lines.show: After products, workers, stores and taxes, only about 3¢ per $1 is left.

scenes.label: paid just for the right to shop there

lines.say: The big money is the card in your wallet.
lines.show: The big money is the card in your wallet.

lines.say: Membership fees brought in five point nine billion dollars.
That's equal to about half of Costco's operating profit, what it earns from running the business.
lines.show: That's equal to about half of Costco's operating profit, what it earns from running the business.

scenes.label: of U.S. and Canada members renew

lines.say: And people keep paying. About ninety-two percent of members in the U.S. and Canada renew.
lines.show: And people keep paying. About 92% of members in the U.S. and Canada renew.

scenes.heading: The Costco playbook
items: Fees bring in money every year

lines.say: Low prices keep members renewing. Renewals bring in money every single year.
lines.show: Low prices keep members renewing. Renewals bring in money every single year.

scenes.takeaway: Low prices bring you in. The membership pays the bills.
